sources.supports: updateVariable validates the variable identifier, posts to update_variable/{variable_id} with the payload as the JSON body and parses the reply with VariableSchema. The payload is passed through unexamined: no public method parses UpdateVariablePayloadSchema, so every payload rule is enforced at the MCP boundary alone.

UpdateVariablePayloadSchema declares name optional and nothing else, and records that an empty body is intentionally accepted as a no-op rather than refused client-side, because TestRail itself accepts it and returns the unchanged variable.

update_variable updates an existing variable; its parameter table carries variable_id alone, marked required, and the article states the request body has the same format as add_variable. The documented response fields are id and name. The documented 400 causes are an invalid or missing variable_id, an invalid variable name, and a variable name that already exists within the project. 403 covers insufficient project permissions, no add/edit permission for Test Data within the project, and "Not an Enterprise license/subscription".

input_policy.notes: One identifier in the path and a body of exactly one documented optional field. An unknown body field is refused, including the id the article's add_variable example shows and its parameter tables never list. Whether the new name is free within the project is TestRail's rule and its refusal arrives from upstream.

outer_result.notes: TestRail answers with the variable, which carries an identifier and a name only. TestRail documents nothing about what a rename does to the values datasets already give the variable, and the reply carries only the variable itself, so this manifest records no outcome for them. The write payloads key values by variable name rather than by identifier, which makes the question a real one rather than an obviously safe rename. Entity-field drift is advisory.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Reject an unknown body field, including the id the article's example shows and TestRail assigns.
Accept an empty body and send it unchanged, which TestRail treats as a no-op returning the unchanged variable, rather than refusing it locally.

parameters.semantics: The variable to update. No coercion; passed positionally and sent verbatim as the only path segment.

wire.encoding: Decimal integer path segment; numeric strings are rejected rather than coerced.

parameters.semantics: No coercion. The JSON object is passed as the driver's second argument and sent unchanged. The object itself is required even though the one field in it is optional, so a no-op is written out as an empty object rather than left implicit.

requirements.description: Preserve the object at driver argument 1 as the JSON request body.
Reject a body that is not an object before driver invocation.

parameters.semantics: A new name for the variable. No coercion; TestRail owns the format and the uniqueness rule within the project.

requirements.description: Preserve the value under its own name.
Reject a non-string value before driver invocation.
Send no name key when the caller did not supply one, so the variable keeps the name it has.
